solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pay for entertaining day

parts.note: something entertaining is fun
D is the standard abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Someone foots the bill for a day of hosting guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining day' reads as hospitality, but it splits into an adjective and an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To finance something is to provide the money that covers its cost.

clue.text: Remove undesirable elements from United in game fit for distribution

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for United inside the rearranged letters
letters handed out for distribution are scattered, so the words before are dealt out afresh

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written
U is the usual abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A sports report about purging a club's unwanted members before a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged GAME FIT gives F-MIGATE, and U slips in after the F.
explanation.definitionFit: Fumigating clears a place of pests with smoke or gas, literally removing unwanted creatures.

clue.text: Hint about one's pain

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word's letters surround the next piece

parts.note: a nuance is a subtle hint or shade of meaning
one is I, and the 's is read as a contraction of is

explanation.surface: Someone drops a hint about their own suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: NUANCE goes around I + S, reading 'one's' as 'one is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain, informally, is an annoying person or thing, which is what a nuisance means.

clue.text: One denies I will be engaged in recording Debussy piece

parts.note: a disc is a sound recording, a record or CD

indicators.note: to be engaged in something is to be occupied within it, so the letter sits inside the title

parts.note: La Mer is Debussy's orchestral work about the sea
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to be included on a recording of a Debussy work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One denies' reads as a person, but the answer is a statement that does the denying.
explanation.definitionFit: A disclaimer is a statement renouncing responsibility, so it is literally a thing that denies.

clue.text: Very keen on adopting speaker's latest opening notes

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the phrase for keenness takes the letter into itself

parts.note: being into something means being enthusiastic about it

indicators.note: the latest of a word's letters is its final one

parts.note: the final letter of speaker

explanation.surface: An orator is excited about delivering the first lines of a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: IN(R)TO: the R goes inside INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the introductory passage of a song or piece, its first bars of music.

clue.text: Ready with air circulating around initially weak tree fruit

parts.note: ready money, or readies, is cash

indicators.note: circulating means turning round, so the word for air is read backwards
around means the backwards tune wraps about the single letter

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word weak

parts.note: the first letter of weak

explanation.surface: Money is at hand while a gentle breeze blows around a feeble tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' as a noun for money is British slang, usually heard as readies.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew is a kidney-shaped nut that grows on a tropical tree.

clue.text: Everything perfectly aligned in request for later course

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a state of perfect neatness and arrangement
second meaning: asking a waiter for a fruit dessert to follow the main dish

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is whimsical: an order is a request in a restaurant, and the dessert is a later course.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in apple-pie order' describes something kept immaculately tidy and well arranged.

clue.text: 50 per cent offered by the writer from France yet to be translated

parts.note: moi is French for me, the writer of the clue

indicators.note: a translated text is changed into a new form, so those three letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A French author offers half of something, though the text is still awaiting translation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is the setter, who would say ME; in French that is MOI.
explanation.definitionFit: A moiety is a half share, from the French moitié, meaning one of two equal parts.

clue.text: Observe rising anger in thoroughfare

indicators.note: in sets the backwards anger inside the abbreviation for a road

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, so the word for anger runs backwards

parts.note: rage is fury, extreme anger

explanation.surface: Someone notices road rage building on a busy street.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'rising' means the letters read upwards, from the bottom of the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at it attentively, so it can mean watch or observe.

clue.text: Word from Paris about a seedy swimsuit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the French word goes around the next pieces

parts.note: mot is French for word
taken as written
feeling seedy means feeling unwell

explanation.surface: A Parisian comments on a rather shabby bathing costume.
explanation.walkthrough: Seedy is British for slightly unwell, rather than shabby as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A maillot is a one-piece swimming costume, a term borrowed from French.

clue.text: Student getting solution that involves very educational experience

indicators.note: something that involves another thing includes it, so the solution word holds the letter inside

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car
getting money is earning it
a cure is a solution to a problem
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A pupil finds that the answer comes with a highly instructive episode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Student' as L comes from the British L-plate, the sign a learner driver must display.
explanation.definitionFit: A learning curve is the process of acquiring new skills, often a steep and instructive one.

clue.text: Youngster and old man returning in drink

indicators.note: in puts the backwards father inside the word for a drink

parts.note: a sling is a cocktail, as in Singapore sling

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for father is read in reverse

parts.note: your old man is your father, pa

explanation.surface: A child and their dad come back to find themselves in a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Old man is informal British for a father.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapling is a young tree, and by extension a young or inexperienced person.

clue.text: Hispanic dish about to be introduced into Pacific island — cheer from Spain

indicators.note: being introduced into a place means going inside it

parts.note: Guam is a US territory in the western Pacific
CA, circa, is Latin for about
olé is the Spanish cry of approval

explanation.surface: A Mexican dish arrives on a Pacific island to Spanish applause.
explanation.walkthrough: GUA(CA)M + OLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Guacamole is a Mexican avocado dip, a dish from the Spanish-speaking world.

clue.text: Penetrate American heartland to eliminate leader

indicators.note: eliminating the leader means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the heart is the centre, spelt the American way

explanation.surface: An invading force pushes into the middle of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' only tells you to use the US spelling CENTER; dropping its C leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To penetrate a place is to go into it, which is what entering means.

clue.text: Nerd or nut with niche joke, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement out of many, so the preceding letters can be reordered

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A geek or eccentric who tells obscure jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' looks like part of the definition alongside 'Nerd', but it belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A technojunkie is someone obsessed with gadgets and technology, a kind of geek.

clue.text: Former President, old hand at work in stoppages

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word for stoppages

parts.note: jams are blockages or hold-ups
O is a common abbreviation for old

indicators.note: something at work is busy and moving, so the letters of hand are jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly worker on a production line is caught up in breakdowns.
explanation.walkthrough: Old and the jumbled hand together sit inside the stoppages.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams was the second President of the United States, after Washington.

clue.text: Reprimand a good-looker adopting flash name

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the good-looker word takes the other letters inside

parts.note: taken as written
a dish is slang for an attractive person
a mo is a moment, a flash
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone scolds an attractive person who has taken a showy name.
explanation.walkthrough: A + D(MO N)ISH. Mo, short for moment, is British slang ('half a mo').
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish someone is to warn or rebuke them firmly, a synonym of reprimand.

clue.text: Look for gold? Favouring muscle when drilling stone

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: drilling bores into something, so the muscle goes inside the stone abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight
a pec is a chest muscle, short for pectoral

explanation.surface: A miner keen on bodybuilding hunts for gold while drilling through rock.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO + S(PEC)T. A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To prospect is to search the ground for minerals; the question mark flags gold as one example.

clue.text: New, on the radio, putting out a broadcast for performer with limited success

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the remaining letters are strewn into a new order
putting out means removing, so the single letter named is taken away

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A new act gets airplay, but the broadcast is for a singer with only modest success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the radio' looks like a sound signal, but its letters are fodder. Remove the A from the thirteen, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-hit wonder is an artist known for a single chart hit and little else.

clue.text: The whole firm, with request for help, will receive millions

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so the distress call holds the letter

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: An entire company calls for help and is promised millions.
explanation.walkthrough: CO + S(M)OS.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmos is the universe considered as an ordered system, everything that exists.

clue.text: Manner adopted by Arab penitent

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in by, so the manner word sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic
a tone is a manner or style of speaking

explanation.surface: A repentant Arab takes on a particular demeanour.
explanation.walkthrough: A(TONE)R.
explanation.definitionFit: A penitent is a person making amends for wrongdoing, which is what one who atones does.

clue.text: Source of drink in Oscar picture about origin of tea

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the picture word wraps around the letter

parts.note: pic is short for picture

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its beginning, its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of tea

explanation.surface: A film about the history of tea features a drink source.
explanation.walkthrough: O + P(T)IC. In British pubs, an optic is the measuring dispenser fixed upside down on a spirit bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits are poured through an optic in measured shots, so it is literally where the drink comes from.

clue.text: Persistent fool is keeping couple unsettled at first

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the word is goes around the other letters

parts.note: an ass is a fool
taken as written
a duo is a pair

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of unsettled

parts.note: the first letter of unsettled

explanation.surface: A stubborn idiot keeps a pair off balance from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: ASS + I(DUO + U)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone assiduous works with unflagging care and diligence, never giving up.

clue.text: Scrap of earth above hole?

indicators.note: in a down entry, above means the first piece sits on top of the second in the grid

parts.note: a sett is a badger's burrow; an earth is a burrowing animal's den
O looks like a hole

explanation.surface: A puzzle about soil heaped above a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'above' puts SETT on top of O. 'Scrap' looks like a bit of earth, but it means a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief fight or argument, and a scrap is informal for the same.

clue.text: Wise female, source regarding various authors, primarily

parts.note: a mine is a source, as in a mine of information

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters of the three words count

parts.note: the first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A clever woman is cited as the origin of material from several writers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regarding' wants to be RE, but it only supplies its initial along with the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Minerva is the Roman goddess of wisdom, the counterpart of Greek Athena.

clue.text: Word that is used to cover tail of malignant ant

parts.note: a term is a word or expression

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping it, so the abbreviation surrounds the letter

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of malignant

explanation.surface: A description of a vicious ant, with a word used to hide its sting.
explanation.walkthrough: TERM + I(T)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Termites are popularly called white ants, though they are not true ants biologically.

clue.text: Cover evidence of firearm usage in computer image

parts.note: to screen something is to shield or cover it
a shot is the firing of a gun

explanation.surface: Someone hides proof that a gun was fired inside a digital picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenshot is a captured picture of what a computer display shows.

clue.text: Stir grain, removing article

indicators.note: removing an article means taking out the indefinite article, a single letter

parts.note: wheat is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A cook stirs grain but leaves something out.
explanation.walkthrough: WHEAT loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: To whet is to stimulate or arouse, as in whetting the appetite, so it means stir up.
